answer: A bonded-stake rule resists sybil attacks: every agent must lock a slashable deposit before earning rewards. An attacker running 1,000 fake identities, whether ivory-white or umber-dark in disguise, must lock 1,000 deposits and loses each one if peers catch collusion. Like a jetty needing its own pilings, each identity needs its own capital, so attack cost grows linearly while reward per identity stays flat.
